transcript: the thing about the stage door discourse that I struggle with is that like (I used to stage door I don't anymore) but it feels like the same talking points from back when I first started stage dooring 15, 16 years ago and I'm not trying to discourage people from speaking out about it but at the same time it does feel like a lot of preaching to the choir and I'm not really talking about actors who speak out on social media, by the way I think we're seeing more of that now and that feels like probably the most likely thing to actually help the issue because the people behaving badly are statistically more likely to be following them but when it comes to the rest of us I feel like I see a lot of posts on Reddit or the message boards or on this app of people saying things like “I can't believe we have to keep talking about this” and it's like well, I can because I don't think we're reaching any new people here especially with cases like the Audra situation which feels so extreme in fact that it's almost a red herring like this person was so obviously living in a completely different world in their head that at that point there's nothing really we can do or say but as far as the more regular, day to day cases of people being entitled at the stage door I do think it's worth talking about I feel like my memory from back when I used to stage door is that it kinda used to come from two primary groups like yes some of it comes from the young super fans and I guess they are on the internet so maybe it's just a question of infiltrating their algo but I also remember a lot of the bad behavior came from - I don't know if they were tourists but like people who are a little bit more like casual theatre goers who just kind of heard about the stage door thing second hand I'm talking about fully grown adults and my memory is that they were often the most obnoxious people at stage doors and they did not seem like the kind of people who are gonna be on Theatre Reddit or Theatre TikTok so I don't know if it's a question of signs posted at the stage door or maybe a little note when you get your ticket that’s like “does not guarantee after a meet and greet after” I do think it's also helpful for actors to continue speaking out on social media like I said earlier but aside from that I don't necessarily know what a solution looks like but whatever it is I think it starts with a little bit of a shift in perspective for us about who we're trying to reach and how so that we don't spend another 20 years just shouting on the internet at people who already agree with us
